{{Quote|This appears to be a collection of ''magical formulas''&hellip;|Aleema Keto|<ref name="FNU1" />}}
A '''Sith spellbook''' was a book that was usually prepared by an individual well versed in [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] lore, and contained the spells, rituals, and incantations necessary for conjuring [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith sorcery]].

==History==
The use of Sith spellbooks dates back as early as the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="people" />

In the year [[3998 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> two young aristocrats from the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Empress Teta system]] named [[Satal Keto/Legends|Satal]] and [[Aleema Keto]] also came to possess a Sith spellbook when they stole one from the [[Galactic Museum/Legends|Galactic Museum]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. It was written in the [[Sith (language)|Sith]] language, and since the Ketos were unable to decipher it, they traveled to Onderon after learning of potential [[darksider]]s who could.<ref name="FNU1" /> They eventually met up with [[King/Legends|King]] [[Ommin/Legends|Ommin]], who gave Satal an [[Sith talisman/Legends|amulet]] that allowed him to completely understand the ancient Sith writings.<ref name="nadd2" />

Roughly [[90 BBY/Legends|three thousand years later]], [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], the only [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] to have survived the [[New Sith Wars]], found the [[Tomb of Freedon Nadd]] during his search for knowledge regarding the creation of [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]]. He successfully penetrated the chamber within the tomb that housed [[Freedon Nadd's holocron]], and after studying the device for many days, found that within were spells for harnessing the intricacies of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith sorcery]]. Because Bane himself was not attuned to Sith sorcery, he transcribed the holocron's data into a spellbook and presented it to his apprentice, [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]].<ref name="ROT" />
